correctness.rationale: State transitions T0(a,b,c)=(a+1,b,c+b) and T1(a,b,c)=(a,b+a,c) compute all counted scattered subsequences. The exact integer identity c=a*b-sum(l_j^2) gives the parity obstruction. Finite-order transitions permit inverse words; commutators C and D shift (b,c) and c by explicitly proven amounts, giving every triple obeying the sole obstruction. Outputs after epsilon, 0 and 10 uniquely recover c,b,a, proving minimality. The proof applies for every m>=2; a standalone checker passed 147447 word comparisons, 22 modular reachability searches, 58751 distinct signature states and 2685 generator/witness checks and 9 independent Moore minimizations.

value.rationale: For an alternating length-three scattered pattern, the first return to the initial symbol produces a nonobvious parity restriction in the natural three-counter machine. The exact quotient \(m^3/\gcd(m,2)\), constructive reachability for every allowed triple and three fixed distinguishing suffixes settle a complete natural invariant for all moduli. The phenomenon is a structural odd/even boundary rather than an arbitrary finite numeric increment. The result provides a benchmark for modular subword-statistics machines, although it does not assert complexity consequences for all patterns.
